info.name: BidForge — Auction Engine API
info.description:
Complete request collection for the BidForge auction backend.

## Before you start
1. Start the database:  docker compose --env-file .env -f docs/docker-compose.yml up -d
2. Start the API:       cd bidforge && ./mvnw spring-boot:run

## How to use it
Run the folder **1 Auth** first — its login requests save JWTs into collection variables, and everything else reads them. After that any folder can be run on its own, or run the whole collection top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner: every request carries its own assertions, so you get a green checklist.

Seeded accounts: admin/Admin@123, and seller1 / bidder1 / bidder2, all Password@123.

Folder **5 Error showcase** deliberately triggers every error the API can produce (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422) to show the single consistent JSON error shape. Folder **6 Full demo flow** tells the whole story in order: create → open → rejected low bid → bidding war → close → winner → audit trail.

request.description: Only the owner may edit, and only while the auction is still SCHEDULED.
Owner (or admin) opens it early. Normally the backend scheduler does this by itself when the start time arrives.
No token needed — browsing is public. Supports filtering, sorting and paging.
The first bid on an English auction only has to reach the starting price.
Every later bid must beat the current highest by at least minIncrement.
A sealed bid only has to reach the starting price — and you only get one.
Sealed bids are invisible while the auction is open. The server never even reads other people's bids, so nothing can leak.
